extraction.title: Anonymous: Add configurable device limit
extraction.head: implement-device-limits

greptile.text: "This PR implements a configurable device limit feature for anonymous access in Grafana." The summary describes frontend config exposure, backend store changes, and a confidence score of 2/5, citing possible race conditions in device counting, inconsistent time windows in the database layer, and synchronous auth changes in client.go.
Style: the test accesses the internal field `anonStore` directly. Suggests exposing a public method on the service instead of reaching into private fields.
Style: suggests a more specific type such as `number | undefined` for `anonymousDeviceLimit`, instead of plain `undefined`, to match the backend type.
Logic: race condition. Concurrent requests can pass the device count check together and create devices beyond the limit. Suggests a database transaction or lock.
Logic: the time window uses `device.UpdatedAt.UTC()` as the current time bound, which may not match the intended logic. Suggests using `time.Now().UTC()` consistently.
Logic: returning `ErrDeviceLimitReached` when no rows are affected in updateDevice is misleading, since the device may not exist rather than the limit being reached.
